transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Ever since they changed my job around, I’ve sunk into this deep, heavy sadness that I just can’t shake, and it’s getting harder to do anything. It got to the point where I couldn't even manage my daily responsibilities anymore, so my sister had to step in and bring me here today.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has the sadness been present most days even when you are not thinking about the job change?

It's been going on for about three months now, pretty much since they restructured my job. Most days I wake up with this heavy, cinder block feeling on my chest that just doesn't go away. It lingers constantly, making me feel completely hopeless about everything in my life—like my bills and my future—not just when I'm thinking about work.
Have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration?

I’ve completely lost interest in my woodworking and fishing with my buddies, as even thinking about them feels pointless and exhausting. My sleep is a mess too; I toss and turn for hours or wake up at 2 a.m. with my mind spinning about work and bills. On top of that, my appetite is totally gone, and I often skip meals because food just tastes like cardboard.

Since the job change, have your symptoms felt mainly tied to that stressor and your ability to cope with it, or have you also had several weeks where the low mood and loss of interest were present most of the day nearly every day независимо of the stressor?

It definitely turned into a constant, daily burden rather than just a reaction to the job stress. For about three months now, this heavy sadness and complete loss of interest in everything have been there almost every single day, most of the day. Even if I'm not thinking about work, that hopeless feeling just doesn't lift.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself? Also, how much has this been affecting your ability to work, take care of yourself, and do daily activities?

Yes, I've been thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up, and I’ve even pictured driving my truck into a concrete barrier because I'm so exhausted from feeling like this. It has completely ruined my life—I've missed so many shifts that my hours got cut, my sister has to handle my bills and clean my apartment, and I've stopped seeing my friends entirely.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energetic or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and were more talkative, confident, or impulsive than normal?

Yes, I swing into these wild phases where I feel incredibly wired and irritable, popping out of bed after only three hours of sleep feeling like I don't need rest. My thoughts race with big business plans and I talk so fast my sister has to slow me down, especially when I get convinced I'm a genius who can save the whole company. During those times, I'll end up tearing through my apartment reorganizing everything and calling coworkers, driven by a motor I just can't stop.
Have you ever had a period like that lasting at least 4 days, or longer, where you felt unusually energized or irritable with much less need for sleep, racing thoughts, or risky/impulsive behavior?

Yes, those wired and irritable phases have been happening on and off for about three months, ever since they restructured my job. When they hit, they definitely last for several days or even a week at a time where my mind is racing and I barely sleep. It's been a constant back-and-forth since the changes at work.

Have you ever had a period of at least a few days when you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable with much less need for sleep, racing thoughts, or impulsive behavior, even when you were not depressed?

Yes, I absolutely have those times when I swing completely out of the heavy depression and feel weirdly pumped up or highly irritable instead. During those days, I’ll sleep maybe three hours but wake up totally wired, with my thoughts racing like a TV with all the channels on at once.
How long do those unusually energized or irritable periods usually last at a time—are they at least 4 days, or do they last a week or more?

To be honest, I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days because I completely lose track of time when I'm that revved up. Everything just moves so fast that the days blur together, so it's really hard to say.
When you have those unusually energized or irritable periods, do they last at least 4 full days, or do they usually last less than 4 days?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days because I really lose track of time when I'm in those revved-up states. But they do seem to last for several days at a time, so it's likely at least that long.
When you have those revved-up periods, do they last at least 7 days, or do they usually last only 4 to 6 days?

I'm really not sure of the exact number of days, to be honest. When I'm in those revved-up states, I completely lose track of time and everything just blurs together. It's hard for me to say if it's four days or a whole week.
When you have those revved-up periods, do they usually last at least 7 days, or are they more often only 4 to 6 days long?

I'm really not sure about the exact number of days. When I get that revved up, I completely lose track of time and everything just blurs together, so I can't tell you if it's closer to four days or a full week.
When those revved-up periods happen, do they ever last a full week or longer, or are they usually only 4 to 6 days long?
I'm honestly not sure of the exact number of days. When I get into that high state, time gets so blurry that I completely lose track of it. I really can't say if it's a full week or just a few days.
During your revved-up periods, have you ever had to be hospitalized, or had such severe symptoms that other people said you were clearly out of control or unable to function safely?

I've never been hospitalized overnight, but things got so out of hand recently that my sister had to step in and bring me to this clinic because I couldn't manage safely. My manager cut my hours because of my erratic behavior on the sales floor, and my sister had to take over my bills and cleaning because I was completely out of control.
During your revved-up periods, have you ever had symptoms so severe that you needed to be hospitalized, or were you clearly unable to function safely because of them?

No, I’ve never been hospitalized in the past, but these revved-up and crashed states have gotten so severe that I just can't function safely on my own anymore. My sister had to step in to manage my bills and apartment, and she finally brought me to this clinic because I was acting erratically at work, missing shifts, and couldn't take care of myself.

During your revved-up periods, did you ever have symptoms severe enough to require hospitalization, or were they clearly causing major problems like losing touch with reality or being unable to function safely?

I've never been hospitalized, but those high periods definitely caused major problems and made me lose touch with reality. When I'm that revved up, I keep hearing my old district manager's voice telling me I'm a failure and that everyone is laughing at me, even though I know nobody is actually there. My behavior at work and at home got so erratic and unsafe that my sister had to step in, take over my bills, and bring me here to the clinic.

I'm still not completely sure about the exact number of days these high periods last. They just seem to go on for several days at a time where I barely sleep, before I eventually crash back down.

I haven't kept close track of the exact number of days, so I'm not entirely sure. But those high periods definitely last for several days at a time and feel like they go on for quite a while.

I'm really not sure of the exact number of days those high periods last because I've never tracked them on a calendar. But I can tell you that this whole cycle of ups and downs has been going on for about three months now.

I'm still not entirely sure of the exact number of days they last because I tend to lose track of time when I'm feeling so wired. I can only tell you that these ups and downs have been happening on and off over the last three months.
When you hear that voice or feel extremely revved up, do those experiences happen only during your high or depressed mood episodes, or do they ever continue even when your mood is back to normal?

Those times I hear my old district manager's voice only seem to happen when I'm in that revved-up, barely-sleeping mode with all the big ideas. Once I slide back down into that heavy, drained depression, the voice disappears completely, even though I still feel awful.
Do the voice-hearing or other unusual beliefs ever happen when your mood feels normal, or do they only occur during your high or depressed episodes?

No, they never happen when my mood is normal. I only hear that voice when I'm in those high, revved-up phases where I'm barely sleeping and filled with big ideas. When I crash into that heavy depression, or if my mood is more level, the voice disappears completely, even though I still feel terrible.
